comment: BANDWIDTH-EXPLORATION results, measured 2026-09-17. Fixture/method as BENCHMARKS.md (30 s cam720 -> 320x240@24, call settings, structured+range+motion+refresh, keyframe every 120). SSIM = ffmpeg 'All' in yuv444p domain, decoded QOV frames vs the same scaled source frames (scoreboard.py ssim_all method). NOTE: absolute SSIM values are NOT comparable to BENCHMARKS.md section 4 rows (0.809-era numbers came from a reference construction that does not reproduce with the canonical method; internally all rows here share one method and baseline bitrate reproduces 260.1 exactly). All rows encoder-side only; decoders untouched.

knob_sweep_q60_fullframe.verdict: ADOPT combo1 (AC dead-zone 0.75 -> 1.0, block-skip slope x8 -> x16): 260.1 -> 197.9 kbps (-23.9%) at SSIM -0.0082; dominates every stock point except q35 (7.5 kbps cheaper but -0.0061 SSIM; stock spends +14 kbps from q35 to q40 to LOSE 0.0005 SSIM). Per-frame SSIM profile flat (no temporal artifacts); tt and skip-base add nothing on top.

rate_control.verdict: Integral controller (cumulative-budget drift, +-1 q per 6 frames, band 5%, q in [25,85]) regulates to -0.8..+6.4% of target. On homogeneous webcam content it is a wash vs the best static point (no >= +0.01 SSIM win at matched bits -> gate NOT met on this fixture). Burst probe (15 s webcam + 15 s testsrc2): controlled 271.5 vs static 322.6 kbps (-15.8%) with calm-half SSIM unchanged (0.9290 vs 0.9288) — budget reallocation works; +37.9% residual overshoot bounded by the q25 floor. Keep as caller policy on the shipped v3.6 qov_set_quality; worth wiring into the adaptation ladder for heterogeneous content.

rungs_content_ssim.note: letterboxed encoder input (scale+pad), decoded content region cropped and upscaled to 320x240, SSIM vs full-frame source — comparable to full-frame rows

wire_rung160_q60_kn_qoa_speech.note: video 86.6 + QOA 69.0; frames fit single 1180 B packets so 1:3 parity is ~free

rungs_content_ssim.verdict: ADOPT 160x120 as the bottom ladder rung (second downscale stage). At ~150 kbps, 256x192 q60 (0.9185) beats full-frame q40 (0.9142) - resolution is the better low-rate knob. Knobs stack on rungs (160 rung: 104.6 -> 86.6 kbps stock->tuned).

rows.note: dropped frames still cost ~1107 B each — this is a framerate cut, not redundancy removal

frame_skip_offline.verdict: CLOSED dead end (pre-registered): near-static frames already cost only their residual/MV minimum and webcam content has almost none (2/720). Network-driven frame skip in the existing ladder already covers the real use case.
